Rebuilt around your two calls: suggest-only wording help, and a design that generates from a mood prompt plus the letter's own text.

The paper-vs-clay question the last version asked is now moot — the design is generated per letter, so both exist and the writer picks. What replaced it is a sharper question: how quiet does the suggestion have to be before it stops feeling like the app is editing you.

1 · Writing, with suggestionsYou write. The app underlines only what reads unnaturally — tap to see the alternative. Nothing changes until you tap accept.

The one grammatical error is deliberate. Screen 1 flags 생각이 나졌어요 — a genuine conjugation mistake, not a style preference. That is the line I have drawn for what "unnatural wording" means: errors, not voice. If the app also flagged 어색하지만 맞는 표현 — awkward but correct, the phrasing that is your fingerprint — it would be smoothing you, which is the thing the ticket warns against. Worth checking whether that line sits where you want it.
Three things this prototype commits to, all reversible. Nothing auto-applies — no silent fixes, and the count is shown (1곳만 제안했어요) so you can see the app is being restrained rather than trusting it. The design reads the letter, which means the agent touches letter text to generate visuals. It is not writing — but it is the first time anything automated reads a letter for a purpose other than recall, and that is worth naming rather than sliding past. A sealed letter keeps its design forever, which is what makes the archive worth scrolling in ten years.
Still open. Whether a letter is editable after sealing; whether sealed-until-a-date survives as a real feature or was just pretty in a mockup; and what the system prompt actually constrains, which is a real spec question — "stay inside Soft Clay" has to become concrete rules before anyone builds it.
